evidenceClaims.statement: A suspicious extremity soft-tissue mass should reach an experienced sarcoma team before a planned image-guided core biopsy so the biopsy path respects a future surgical approach.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Biopsy technique and selected incisional approaches remain specialist decisions; imaging suspicion is not a tissue diagnosis.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults whose extremity mass remains suspicious after local MRI characterization.

evidenceClaims.statement: MRI is appropriate for local characterization of a deep, enlarging, or ultrasound-indeterminate extremity soft-tissue mass before biopsy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: MRI can characterize and guide planning but cannot by itself prove sarcoma.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with a deep, enlarging, or ultrasound-indeterminate extremity soft-tissue mass.

evidenceClaims.statement: Image-guided core sampling of a heterogeneous soft-tissue tumor should target viable tumor identified with enhancement or vascularity.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Exact targeting is directly supported by older primary technique guidance; current society guidance corroborates planned image-guided core biopsy. No diagnostic certainty from MRI alone, invented needle size or tract rule added.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The adult synthetic clinical scenarios identified in the associated question mappings.

evidenceClaims.statement: Planned sarcoma biopsy should avoid contaminating a separate unaffected compartment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The exact compartment rule is directly checked in older ESSR technique guidance; current SEOM corroborates tract removal/planning. Constructed rectus/adductor and triceps/biceps paths require clinician anatomy review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

evidenceClaims.statement: A feasible image-guided core biopsy is preferred initially for a suspicious deep extremity soft-tissue mass.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Open biopsy is a selected alternative, not universally wrong; no failed core, needle gauge, sample count or tumor subtype is invented.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Rectus femoris belongs to the anterior thigh compartment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Stable anatomy, independently synthesized from the review's compartment depiction. No figure adapted. The exact constructed tract still needs clinician review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Adductor longus is a muscle of the medial thigh compartment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Directly described anatomical membership; not a claim about all adductor variants or the clinical safety of a trajectory. B19's medial crossing is a constructed observation.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Biceps brachii is in the anterior arm compartment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate imaging-anatomy review for stable membership. No source expression adapted; exact case route requires clinician review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Triceps brachii is in the posterior arm compartment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate imaging-anatomy review for stable membership. No source expression adapted; exact case route requires clinician review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Image-guided core biopsy planned with the definitive-treatment team is the preferred initial tissue approach for a suspicious deep soft-tissue mass.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Incisional biopsy can be appropriate after nondiagnostic cores or when core sampling is unsafe. Small superficial excision exceptions do not apply to the constructed deep masses.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: The biopsy tract should be selected so that it can be included safely in the definitive sarcoma resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Constructed corridors still require sarcoma/radiology anatomical confirmation. Tract planning must not become a reason to omit necessary pre-treatment diagnosis.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

A planned image-guided core biopsy can obtain tissue while placing the biopsy tract where it can be managed within a future surgical approach; MRI suspicion alone is not sarcoma confirmation.
sourceLabels: Noebauer-Huhmann et al., ESSR soft-tissue imaging guideline (2024), CC BY 4.0
